Last month, OpenAI publicly demoed a hardware product marketed under the Codex name. Today, the company officially launched its collaboration with Work Louder: a Codex Micro keyboard priced at US$230.

Product introduction as follows:

The keyboard comes in two versions: clicky (blue switch) and silent switch.

The official website states: "Every Agent key lights up with RGB effects based on Codex's status, so you can tell at a glance who's thinking, running, waiting or done before switching conversations."

The product page also lists three Codex-specific features:

  • Instant trigger skills: flick the joystick to launch frequently-used Codex workflows, such as reviewing PRs (Pull Requests), debugging, or refactoring code.
  • Common operations at your fingertips: command keys provide dedicated shortcuts for your most-used actions—accept, reject, push-to-talk, start new conversation, etc.—reducing context switches and boosting productivity.
  • Tune compute intensity: turn the knob to adjust the reasoning level in real time. Stay fast on simple tasks, instantly crank it up when deeper thinking is needed.

Available for order starting today—click here for details. There's also a promotional video:

That's the gist of it. For OpenAI and the hardware world, this month has been a busy one.
